summary: Milestone 2026.05.253 had no experiment commits recorded since activation. Both GPUs (RTX 3090 x2) were idle at 0% utilization with only 5 MB allocated each, consistent with no compute-bound tasks having run. No wall time or throughput data is available for analysis.
bottlenecks_identified: No experiments launched or committed during this milestone — the milestone produced zero throughput. This is the primary bottleneck: the activation-to-first-experiment gap consumed the entire milestone window.
improvements_suggested: Verify conductor activation completed successfully and that research-roadmap-next.yaml was consumed; a zero-experiment milestone typically indicates the conductor stalled at activation rather than at execution.

Check ops/conductor-log.md and ops/conductor-state.json for the last activation event to diagnose whether the planner failed to emit a YAML, the activation guard blocked the milestone, or a doomed-rerun cascade blocked all tasks before launch.

If the zero-experiment outcome was caused by a YAML validation failure, run scripts/exclusion_manifest_lint.py against the rejected roadmap draft to surface the blocking condition before the next milestone is activated.
Both RTX 3090 GPUs are healthy and idle (42C / 45C) — no thermal or hardware issue is responsible. The issue is purely in the planning/activation pipeline, not in compute availability.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Diagnose conductor stall: read ops/conductor-log.md and ops/conductor-state.json to identify whether the milestone was blocked at YAML validation, doomed-rerun check, or another gate — then fix the root cause before activating 2026.05.254.

Pre-stage research-roadmap-next.yaml for milestone 2026.05.254 per the Pre-Staged Roadmap Convention in CLAUDE.md, ensuring all exclusion-manifest cross-checks and principal-annotated artifact fields are present before handing off to the conductor.

Run scripts/exclusion_manifest_lint.py and ops/known-issues.md review jointly before drafting the next roadmap to prevent another cascade-block from a retired experiment_id or a scope-reduction directive being ignored.
meta_reflection: A zero-experiment milestone is a process failure at the orchestration layer, not at the research layer. The GPUs, toolchain, and models are available and healthy; the conductor or planner failed to translate the activation into launched work. The retrospective framework correctly surfaces this as a pipeline bottleneck rather than attributing it to slow individual experiments — that distinction matters for the next corrective action.
